paragraphs: Friend, here's what David teaches me in Psalm 4: you can pray before you've got anything figured out. He opens with "Answer me when I call, O God of my righteousness!" and he doesn't clean up his words first (Psalm 4:1). He's got people running down his honor, and he takes it straight to God, who he says has already "relieved" his distress (Psalm 4:1). If David can bring the mess to God, so can you, even when it's a MESS.

Now watch what David does with the noise around him. Many are asking, "Who can show us the good?" and David answers with a prayer: "Shine the light of Your face upon us, O LORD" (Psalm 4:6). He says the LORD "has set apart the godly for Himself" and "hears when I call to Him" (Psalm 4:3). Even his anger gets a plan: "Be angry, yet do not sin; on your bed, search your heart and be still" (Psalm 4:4). So when life gets loud, the good isn't out in the crowd, friend. It's in the LORD.

And that's where the peace comes from. David says, "You have filled my heart with more joy than when grain and new wine abound" (Psalm 4:7). Then he ends with "I will lie down and sleep in peace, for You alone, O LORD, make me dwell in safety" (Psalm 4:8). His peace doesn't rest on a quiet day or a full pantry. It rests on the LORD ALONE, so tonight, baker, you can hand Him the whole day and sleep.
